title: The link check reads the loader too, and proves Fabric in a client
text: A mod links against its loader as well as the game: NeoForge's own classes with FML and its event bus, Fabric Loader and Fabric API. The scoreboard only read the game (and NeoForge's own classes), so a loader API change was a surprise at load time (Explorer's and Nature's Compass on 1.20.6 -> 1.21, ModLoadingContext.registerConfig). The snapshot gets every library NeoForge's own pom lists, and Fabric Loader and Fabric API with the interfaces Fabric API adds to game classes; loader breaks are ranked with game ones. The shared cache under ~/.mmt/exposure is keyed by the content of the tools that built it, so worktrees running at once cannot break each other (#126). exposure.py load starts ported Fabric mods in a real Fabric client too (its intermediary names translated for mmt's agent).
finish: port.jar-links.every-update counts 21 NeoForge updates; loader API breaks are counted in the scoreboard; Fabric load on 1.21.1 -> 1.21.2 reports server and client and every linked standalone mod loads in both; two worktrees running exposure.py jars at once both give correct results
wrongIf: a mod the link check clears fails on a real server or client on a loader member
result: 2026-11-20: port.jar-links.every-update counts 64 updates, 21 of them NeoForge: 5,826 of 9,423 mod ports link (61.8%). On the 61 updates main measured it goes 5,775 -> 5,586. Linking against the loader (NeoForge with FML and its event bus, Fabric Loader and Fabric API) costs 28 net (NeoForge -28, Fabric 0 once mods' bundled copies of Fabric API modules, which never run, stop counting); the biggest are FML's FMLEnvironment.dist becoming a method (64 NeoForge mods on 1.21.8 -> 1.21.9), Fabric API's 26.1 renames (PayloadTypeRegistry, KeyBindingHelper), NeoForge 20.6 removing Event.Result, and Explorer's and Nature's Compass on ModLoadingContext.registerConfig. 165 more stop counting as linking because their game code is in a jar their own loader unpacks, which the port never reads (Essential, Crash Assistant, CustomSkinLoader, about 3 per update): they are reported as not read. Loader breaks are labelled and counted per update (loaderUses, modsHeldOnlyByLoader): 5,654 uses, 151 mod ports held by nothing else. The cache under ~/.mmt/exposure is keyed by tool content: two worktrees with different tools running Fabric 1.19.2 -> 1.19.3 at once both gave 38 of 150 and 2,546 broken uses, as the cloud did. Fabric load 1.21.1 -> 1.21.2 now starts a real Fabric client (Fabric's launcher profile; mmt's agent reads intermediary through Mojang's and Fabric's mappings): 13 standalone mods link; on the server 7 of 7 that a server runs load (6 are client-only), and in the client 12 of 13 load. Better Mount HUD links and fails in the client: its @ModifyVariable finds no target in 1.21.2's HUD code, an injection point the link check does not read yet (step 55). Essential, which linked before and failed in the client on a removed class, is now counted as not read.
